summary: A DAK's web annexes held beside an IG's artefact index: its core data dictionary workbook as JSON (`dak-data-dictionary/v1`, loaded on demand by the IG site's annex view), and the declared mapping from its generic personas to the swimlanes of its business-process figures (`dak-swimlanes/v1`).

avatar.reads: a page with a folded corner and rows — an annex to the guideline, held as data

rationale: smart-base's own kind, NOT families added to fhir-harness's `fhir-artifact-index`. Both formats are DAK concepts (a DAK's data dictionary; a DAK's personas against its business-process swimlanes), and fhir-harness may know nothing about WHO (`check:fhir-harness-exclusions`), so listing them on fhir-harness's kind would put WHO names in fhir-harness. The registry joins a validator only onto a family its kind lists, so the files need a kind that lists them: this one. `derived`: each file is written by a smart-base script from the DAK's own source (the workbook; the personas page and the process figures plus a declaration of aliases) and regenerated, never edited by hand except the swimlane declaration's aliases, which the script reads and does not write. Found 2026-10-11 by `check:kind-validators:require-all`, which reported both families unmapped while they sat in `fhir-artifact-index/`.
